name: Zmey (Slavic Dragon)
description: The zmey (Russian zmei, Ukrainian zmiy, Polish żmij, Serbian/Croatian/Slovenian zmaj, Bulgarian zmei) is the dragon of Slavic mythology — a flying, often multi-headed, fire-breathing serpent that shapeshifts between dragon and human form, with sharply different moral roles in East Slavic and South Slavic traditions.

aliases.name: Zmey Gorynych
aliases.meaning: the Serpent Gorynych — multi-headed dragon of the bylinas

regions: East Slavic lands (Russian and Ukrainian folktale and bylina traditions)
Western Balkans (Serbian, Croatian, Slovenian zmaj traditions)
Bulgaria and North Macedonia (zmei and lamia traditions)
Poland (żmij and the Wawel Dragon of Kraków)
origin: Pan-Slavic. The zmey is documented across the Slavic-speaking world: East Slavic (Russia, Ukraine, Belarus), South Slavic (Bulgaria, Serbia, Croatia, North Macedonia, Slovenia), and West Slavic (Poland, Czech, Slovak) traditions, with related figures in Romania.
